correctness.independent_verification: Independently built the six conic-evaluation rows from coordinates (0:1:1),(1:0:1),(u:1:0),(1:1:1),(u:1:1),(u:1:u) and used direct exact symbolic determinant: det M(u)=u²(u−1)². Independently checked the Bézout equations 2a=12, a+3b=15 giving (a,b)=(6,3). Source verify.py also enumerates 120 labeled 3-triple incidence descriptions; the universal proof is the incidence and symbolic determinant argument.
correctness.rationale: In CP2 six distinct lines have total pair intersections 15 and a smooth conic has total line-conic intersections 12. Ordinary triple-only incidence forces six conic-plus-two-line triples and three line-only triples. Nine line–triple incidences over three distinct triple points force exactly the sides of a projective triangle and a single additional cevian through each vertex. Normalize axes x=0,y=0,z=0 and cevians y=z,z=x,x=uy with u≠0,1. All six remaining ordinary line double intersections must lie on the conic. Their homogeneous quadratic evaluation matrix has exact polynomial determinant u²(u−1)², nonzero for all admissible u, forbidding even reducible conics. The projective normalization accounts for distinctness/nonconcurrency; no sample-parameter argument substitutes for this identity.
